the model says the meaning changed: The diff rewrites how the judge question is built for older records: it adds a transcript search for the record's own words (`_own_words`, `_said_in`), takes the date from the transcript message, and writes a "found none of your words" line. That is the quote-with-date or not-found wording that SR-249 EX-1 and EX-2 describe.; brought to the owner as a card: What you asked for: iaso approves a record for you only when it is sure what you meant. Otherwise the judge model asks you, and nothing gets approved just because something else seems to match.

What the requirement says: for an older record iaso never saw you write, iaso looks for its words in messages you typed in this project's past sessions. The judge model's question then either quotes those words with their date (for example "4 Oct") or says they weren't found and asks what you meant. Finding the words doesn't approve anything by itself, and records you've already approved are skipped.

What changed: this change builds that behaviour into how the judge's questions are written. If the judge gives no quote, iaso now looks up the older record's own words in your past sessions and shows them with the day they were said. If nothing is found, it adds the line "I found none of your words about this in your past sessions." Nothing in the change approves a record because of a match. The change seems to do what the requirement describes, so I can't say it broke anything.

What's unclear:
- No request from you is on file for when this change was made, so I can't tell if you asked for it.
- When nothing is found, iaso only adds the "found none" line. Asking what you meant is left to the judge model's own question.
- The change also searches past sessions for quotes on newer records, while the requirement only describes doing that for older ones.
- Questions you've already answered are now dropped, and the record keeps waiting. The cut-off for question headers also changed.

the model says the meaning changed: EX-2 says the repin step refusing a link pinned to a reworded requirement writes a debug case naming the link and refusal, but the change now skips opening a case when the refusal is REWORDED.; brought to the owner as a card: You want iaso to open a debug case whenever one of its steps refuses something it should handle. The requirement gives an example of this: when the repin step refuses a decision pinned to a requirement that was reworded, iaso writes a debug case, and you are asked nothing (EX-2).

The code change does the opposite for exactly that case. When the refusal is because the requirement was reworded, the stale check now skips the debug case. A comment in the code says the refusal is "by design" and should go to you as a card. Other refusals still open debug cases.

Your intent doesn't settle which view is right. It only says "a step refuses what it should handle". Whether the repin step should handle a link to a reworded requirement, or whether that is a normal refusal you should look at, is a decision only you can make. the model says the meaning changed: fix() and handle() now return early and resolve a stale-refused case whose detail is the reworded requirement, without running any round, worktree, test, judge review or commit, which the statement says every failing-rerun case goes through.; brought to the owner as a card: The requirement and your intent agree on this: when a debug case's rerun fails again, iaso works it through to a fix in its own worktree and branch, with a failing test, green tests, repinned links and a judge review. A case counts as resolved only when its branch holds that fix.

The code change adds an exception. A "stale-refused" case is one opened because iaso refused to repin a stale link. If that refusal happened because the requirement was reworded, iaso now closes the case straight away as the owner's call (the code points to SR-325, the reworded-requirement card). No round runs, no branch, no test, no judge review, no commit. The same exception applies in other repositories.

This may well be what you want. Your intent opens cases only for refusals of things a step "should handle", and a refusal made on purpose isn't a defect. But the requirement has no such exception. It also says a case is resolved only when its branch holds a fix, while these cases are now marked resolved with no fix at all.
